equity.level_reason: Only age (kindergartners) defines the population; results are by state, school year and vaccine, none of which is an SPD. A single generic mention of returning coverage 'equitably' does not frame equity.

level_alternative.reason: The Discussion says CDC aims to restore coverage 'as quickly and equitably as possible', which could be read as equity raised as a recommendation.

equity.equity_measurement: No SPD analyzed; comparisons are across states, school years and exemption types; school type (public/private/homeschool) is a weighting stratum, not an SPD.

notes: Design is not named; surveillance/descriptive plus trend inferred from annual state reporting and the year-over-year headline. Lower-bound exemption estimates for states reporting per-vaccine exemptions are a fixed fill-in rule, not a procedure. Comparisons with the 95% Healthy People target and 5% exemption threshold enter through potentially achievable coverage.
view_issues: Summary says exemptions increased in 41 states, while Abstract and Results say 40 states and DC. Implications says 48 states in 2020–21 vs 40 in 2022–23 could reach 95%, while Results compares with 'all but four states' in 2021–22.
